statements.t: The Company is one of the largest mineral resource holders in the state with a pipeline of three underground and two open pit projects strategically located in some of Nevada's most prolific gold-producing trends.

• Net loss increased to $48.4 million compared to $41.9 million in the prior year period, due primarily to higher pre-development, evaluation and exploration costs incurred as the Company advances multiple projects within its development plan.

• Net loss was $179.5 million compared to $113.3 million in the prior year period, due to higher pre-development, evaluation and exploration expenses as the Company advances multiple projects within its development plan and higher non-cash fair value revaluation losses on a net basis partially offset by higher gross profit.

Gross proceeds of $662.5 million and net proceeds of $637.2 million were received on closing, which completed the recapitalization plan ahead of the Company's mid-2026 target to support the development plan:

• On September 21, 2026, the Company announced the results of a feasibility study for Granite Creek underground supported by two technical reports: (1) a technical report prepared under National Instrument 43-101 - Standards of Disclosure for Mineral projects which, in the opinion of the qualified persons, constitutes a feasibility study under NI 43-101, and (2) a technical report summary prepared under Subpart…

Development of the Company’s two large, open pit oxide projects (Mineral Point and Granite Creek), as well as its third underground mine (Cove), are expected to follow to support a long-term target of 500,000 to 600,000 3 ounces of annual gold output.

In support of the multi-phase development plan, the Company released Preliminary Economic Assessments prepared in accordance with NI 43-101 and a corresponding Initial Assessment prepared under S-K 1300, each published in the first quarter of 2025 (the "2025 PEA"), covering all five gold projects.
On October 14, 2026, the Company updated its development plan to better align plant feed and processing capacity, and optimize capital allocation.
While the Company’s operating and near-term development projects remain on their initial schedule, the sequence of medium-to-long term projects has been updated as follows:

All of the Company’s projects, except Granite Creek underground are considered exploration stage projects under S-K 1300 because the Company has not determined mineral reserves at any of its properties pursuant to S-K 1300.

At Archimedes underground, the Company expects the oxide mineralization to expand based on recently published drill results from the upper 426 zone, and continues to drill within the lower 426 and Ruby Deeps zones (see the Company’s June 25, 2026 press release).

Together, these results continue to support the Company’s view that the mineralized bodies at both Granite Creek underground and Archimedes underground remain open for potential expansion and are expected to sufficiently supply the Lone Tree Plant with material feed for a significant period of time and longer than previously contemplated.
This revised sequence of development projects provides an opportunity for the Company to prioritize the Mineral Point open pit project, which is the Company’s largest and most valuable asset.

The exploration program, early-stage pre-permitting activities, technical studies, metallurgical test work, and engineering are ongoing and continue to improve the Company’s understanding of the deposit to support future project planning.

Mineral Point is the Company’s largest development project by mineral resource, estimated valuation and anticipated annual production, and represents a key driver of anticipated future production growth for the Company.

Parallel to the updated development plan, the Company has optimized its processing strategy where a large portion of refractory material from the Granite Creek and Archimedes underground projects is expected to be stockpiled in 2027 for processing at the Company's wholly owned Lone Tree Plant once commissioned, rather than processed through a third-party facility.

These financings completed the Company's broader recapitalization plan ahead of its mid-2026 target and align with the projected capital requirements and cash flows of the current project development plan.

All of the Company’s projects other than Granite Creek underground are considered exploration stage projects under S-K 1300, as the Company has not determined mineral reserves at such properties pursuant to S-K 1300.
The Company’s 2026 production, operating and pre-development evaluation and exploration expense guidance are summarized below:
The Company expects to be largely within its guidance ranges published in its Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025, on February 19, 2026.
The Company’s expectations for 2026 have changed from that guidance as follows:

This is in part due to the decision to leach Archimedes oxide material on our existing leach pad rather than selling it under the ore purchase agreement, which is expected to delay recording production from the fourth quarter of 2026 to the first quarter of 2027.
The original guidance assumed a gap between commitment and invoicing/payment of 30 days, in practice, the Company is experiencing between four to five months for this timing difference.
The Company continues to expect the refurbishment capital to be nearly fully committed by year-end.

This outlook, including expected results and targets, is subject to various risks, uncertainties and assumptions, which may impact future performance and the Company’s ability to achieve the results and targets discussed in this section.
The Company may, but is under no obligation to, update this outlook depending on changes in metal prices and other factors.
The Company anticipates executing the accordion feature in the first half of 2027, at which point the number of additional gold ounces to be delivered will be determined.
The Company expects the total ounces to be delivered for the $250 million facility to represent approximately 15% of total gold output over the projected period of January 2028 to June 2030.
Granite Creek underground is the Company's first brownfield project to be redeveloped and is currently ramping up towards steady-state gold output.
The Company expects full-year production for the project to be within its guidance range.
The Company expects over half of the material at the third-party facility to be processed by the end of 2026.
Drilling progressed slower than anticipated during the quarter due to water management and insufficient contractor personnel to maintain continuous operations.
The Company is currently working through operational permitting needs followed by the an expected NEPA permitting process, which is currently projected to commence in 2027.

The Ruby Hill property includes the Archimedes underground project, the Company's second planned underground mine for which construction began during 2025, and the Mineral Point open pit, which is a large oxide gold and silver deposit with the potential to become the Company’s largest gold producing asset.
During the first quarter of 2025, the Company finalized a PEA for the Ruby Hill property covering both Archimedes underground and Mineral Point open pit projects.

The Company’s updated development plan prioritizes the Mineral Point open pit as the Company’s next major development project to drive the next phase of production growth following the anticipated establishment of its underground hub-and-spoke mining and processing platform.
Cove is an advanced stage exploration project and is expected to be the Company's third underground mine.
During the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company continued to advance technical and economic studies for the Cove Underground project.

Demonstrated resource expansion potential at Granite Creek and Archimedes, the Company's first two underground projects, has provided the flexibility to sequence Cove underground later in the development pipeline as an important future source of refractory feed to the Lone Tree Plant, when future mining rates decline at the first two underground mines.

The Lone Tree property contains the Lone Tree Plant and a historic producing mine that ceased mining operations in 2006 and is located within the Battle Mountain-Eureka Trend, midway between the Company's Granite Creek property and Cove underground project.
Upon refurbishment and commissioning, the Lone Tree Plant is intended to allow the Company to transition from toll milling to owner-operated processing.
During the first quarter of 2026, the Company provided Hatch Associates Consultants, Inc., with a formal Notice to Proceed ("NTP") for the Lone Tree refurbishment project.
The Company continues to expect the refurbishment capital to be nearly fully committed by year-end, and the project remains on schedule.
The Company expects all major procurement and contracts to be in place by the end of 2026 providing greater certainty around the projected cost to complete the project.

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company incurred higher pre-development, evaluation and exploration expenses, compared to the prior year period reflecting the increased activity to advance key development milestones across all five gold projects within its development plan.

Additional liquidity is available through the remaining $25 million from the NSR Royalty, subject to satisfaction of specified project expenditure conditions, the $100.0 million accordion feature under the 2026 Gold Prepay, and future proceeds from warrant exercises as well as the Company is in dialogue with its lead lenders to establish a corporate revolving credit facility, if needed.

Pursuant to the terms of the Silver Purchase Agreement, which commenced as of April 30, 2022, the Company is to deliver to Orion 100% of the silver production from the Granite Creek and Ruby Hill projects until the delivery of 1.2 million ounces of silver, after which the delivery will be reduced to 50% until the delivery of an aggregate of 2.5 million ounces of silver, after which the delivery will be reduced to…

The obligations under the Silver Purchase Agreement are secured obligations of the Company and its wholly-owned subsidiaries Ruby Hill Mining Company LLC, and Osgood Mining Company LLC, and secured against the Ruby Hill project in Eureka County, Nevada and the Granite Creek project in Humboldt County, Nevada.
The 2023 Gold Prepay Accordion will be repaid through the delivery by the Company to Orion of 13,333 ounces of gold.

estimates.t: Critical accounting policies and estimates used to prepare our financial statements are discussed with our audit committee as they are implemented.

statements.t: “We delivered another solid quarter, with increased production from Granite Creek as the project continued to ramp up on plan, the advancement of Archimedes on schedule toward becoming our second underground mine, and the start of demolition at the Lone Tree Plant,” stated Richard Young, President & CEO.
Our success year-to-date demonstrates the Company’s ability to advance multiple projects concurrently.

We remain on track to commence gold mining at Archimedes and major construction at Lone Tree in the fourth quarter of this year, marking two important milestones by year-end as we execute our development plan to build a Nevada-focused mid-tier gold producer.”
The Company remains on track to achieve its full year production guidance range.

• Net loss increased to $52.5 million compared to $30.2 million in the prior year period, due primarily to higher pre-development, evaluation and exploration costs incurred as the Company advances multiple projects within its development plan.
Over the next 18 months, the Company is targeting the following key catalysts while continuing to identify opportunities to optimize the development schedule:
The Company remains on track to meet its 2026 guidance as originally published in its 2025 Year End Annual Report on Form 10-K on February 19, 2026 subject to the following:

• Lone Tree plant refurbishment capital expenditures are expected to be lower in 2026 than guided, management was conservative in estimating expenditures for Lone Tree during the recapitalization planning process earlier in year to ensure that the Company raised sufficient capital.

Based on positive drill results, management is pivoting from refurbishment of certain existing facilities on site to construction of a new worker change facility and additional offices that are expected to improve operating effectiveness both for Archimedes and Mineral Point.

This outlook, including expected results and targets, is subject to various risks, uncertainties and assumptions, which may impact future performance and the Company’s ability to achieve the results and targets discussed in this section.
The Company may, but is under no obligation to, update this outlook depending on changes in metal prices and other factors.
Granite Creek underground is the Company's first brownfield project to be redeveloped and is currently ramping up towards steady-state gold output.
The Company remains on track to meet its full-year production guidance.
The second water treatment plant will increase surface water treatment capacity to approximately 3,500 gallons per minute to support the Company's long-term groundwater management objectives.
The Company expects the material to be processed during the third quarter of 2026.
Drilling progressed slower than anticipated during the quarter due to water management, maintenance downtime, and rig relocation.

Based on preliminary assessments of potential environmental impacts, the project may require preparation of an Environmental Impact Statement ("EIS") under the Bureau of Land Management ("BLM") process.

The Ruby Hill property includes the Archimedes underground project, the Company's second planned underground mine for which construction began during 2025, and Mineral Point open pit, which is a large oxide gold and silver deposit with the potential to become the Company’s largest gold producing asset.
The Company continues to expect to achieve first gold from Archimedes in the fourth quarter of 2026.

Management expects to increase the overall drilling rate for the remainder of the year with mobilization of additional rigs, however, completion of the drill program is now expected in the first quarter of 2027.
Cove is an advanced stage exploration project and is expected to be the Company's third underground mine.
During the second quarter, the Company continued to advance technical and economic studies for the Cove Underground project.
The project spend is weighted in the second half of the year and the Company expects to meet full-year guidance.

The Company is one of the largest mineral resource holders in the state with a pipeline of three high-grade underground and two open pit projects strategically located in some of Nevada’s most prolific gold-producing trends.

risks.t: beyond the Company’s control, including: general economic and industry conditions
volatility of commodity prices, including the prices of gold and silver
uncertainties related to the refurbishment of the Lone Tree Plant, including cost overruns and construction delays
risks related to third-party toll milling arrangements and processing delays
uncertainties regarding water management and groundwater inflows at Granite Creek
risks related to the conversion of mineral resources and the results of feasibility and other technical studies
risks associated with mineral exploration, development and mining operations generally
risks relating to the reliance on key personnel and contractors (including Hatch)
changes in applicable laws, regulations or government policies in Canada and the United States
foreign exchange and interest rate fluctuations
